standard.name: Standard
standard.blurb: Fair but real. You can lose, but the game tells you why, and you get three quarters of grace before foreclosure.

easy.name: Easy
easy.blurb: Bigger loan, cheaper interest, fewer bad events, no foreclosure. Greyed out in Phase 1.

classic.name: Classic
classic.blurb: Shoestring start and harsh interest, the way old park sims felt. Greyed out in Phase 1.

_notes: debt_cap = debt_cap_base + debt_cap_networth_factor * park assets (land, fences, dinosaurs, buildings at their resale ratios). Borrowed cash never raises the cap; overdrawn cash lowers it. M2.6 fix: the base was below start_loan, so the Bank could lend nothing on day 1 and the day-1 overspend trap was unreachable. Foreclosure now measures NET debt (debt - cash) against the cap, so borrowing to the ceiling and overdrafting feed the same number and a bigger cap does not push the trap further away. Playtest fix: base 60000 -> 88000 -> 100000 and the asset factor 0.6 -> 0.75, so the SPEC scenario (three marquee dinosaurs AND Parking III on day 1, about $148,000) is actually reachable with bank money; at 88000 the Grand Lot was still $10,000 out of reach. The bank hands a reckless owner enough rope, and the overspend run still forecloses on day 271 because net debt ends near $195,000 against a cap that collapses back toward the base once the animals die.
